text:
mikaela: Heads-up — after the RFC review, we still need to pick an approach for span fragment handling. Two concrete options on the table: reassemble fragments at ingress (streaming reassembly) or store lightweight fragments and reassemble at query/analysis time. Tradeoffs thread.

jon: Streaming reassembly seems attractive for correctness and easier downstream consumers — traces arrive as full spans. But worried about increased memory/CPU at the front door and tricky backpressure. :thinking:

grace: Storing fragments+reassembly at query reduces peak ingestion cost but makes real-time alerting & SLO dashboards harder. Also harder to dedupe if fragments duplicate across retries.

chen: We should quantify: what fraction of traces are fragmented today? If it's <1% maybe query-time reassembly plus a small cache is fine. If fragmentation is common, streaming wins.

mikaela: Good point. I pulled a quick sample from raw ingest for last 24h — ~4.2% of traces had >1 fragment, and of those ~30% were retries (dup fragments). I'll paste the query.

mikaela: ```sql
SELECT count(*) AS total,
  sum(case when fragments>1 then 1 else 0 end) AS fragmented
FROM raw_traces_24h;
-- fragmented / total ~ 0.042
```

ingest-bot: Notice: recent deploy added header support for trace-fragment-id: true

jon: 4.2% is non-negligible. With retries causing duplicates, streaming reassembly will need dedupe logic anyway. How expensive is dedupe on the fast path vs on-demand?

grace: Dedupe at ingress: need a short-lived LRU or bloom-filter keyed by (trace_id, fragment_seq) to drop duplicates. Adds memory but bounded TTL ~ 30s. Query-time dedupe: more complex because fragments for same trace may be spread across partitions/time. Requires a more expensive join.

chen: Also consider latency targets: hosted API wants <200ms p50 for trace-backed error analyzers. Query-time reassembly will add a variable delay; streaming can deliver near real-time.

mikaela: Another axis: cost attribution. If we reassemble at ingress we can tag the assembled trace with derived cost buckets and emit a single envelope downstream. Query-time reassembly means cost attribution may be split and harder to aggregate correctly.

jon: What about a hybrid: do streaming reassembly for traces that finish quickly (all fragments arrive within N seconds), otherwise fall back to storing fragments and background reassembly. That reduces steady-state pressure.

grace: I like hybrid. Implementation sketch: keep a small in-memory assembler per shard with TTL 3s; if all fragments arrived -> emit assembled trace; if TTL expires -> flush fragments to object store/fragment table for background reassembly. Background reassembler runs periodically and compacts.

chen: We need to decide data schema for fragments if we go hybrid. Minimal fields: trace_id, fragment_seq, total_fragments (optional), payload_ref (S3/segment), src_region, received_ts, dedupe_key. Avoid duplicating full payload in hot path.

mikaela: Proposed fragment header we already added: `X-Trace-Frag: id=<trace_id>;seq=<n>;total=<m>;dup_key=<uuid>` — keep it short. Hot path stores payload_ref if payload > 32kb.

jon: Error modes: if total is missing (producer didn't set), assembler should still attempt ordering by seq and use TTL. Also define metric labels: assembler_hits, assembler_misses, fragments_flushed_to_store, reassembled_from_store_latency.

grace: Operational concerns: observability for the assembler itself (queue length, GC pauses), and clear SLA with product teams for when traces may be delayed for dashboards. We should add a fallback route: if assembled trace fails schema validation, fall back to fragments store and emit a schema error event.

mikaela: Action items I propose: 1) implement a 3s in-memory assembler prototype on one ingest shard; 2) add fragment schema + header spec doc; 3) add metrics and dashboards for assembler health; 4) run canary for 2 weeks and measure ingestion CPU/mem delta and end-to-end latency.

chen: +1. I'll draft the fragment schema doc and open a PR for header docs.

jon: I'll take the prototype for the assembler and add dedupe bloom filter with 30s TTL. Will instrument counters.

grace: I'll own the canary plan and acceptance criteria (CPU increase <=8%, p50 trace latency change <=10ms, assembled trace success rate >=98%).

mikaela: Great. If anyone else wants to weigh in re: storage format for fragment payload_ref (SST vs object store chunking) please comment here. Otherwise I'll file tickets for the action items. :thumbsup:

ingest-bot: Ticket created: PROJ-894 "Prototype in-memory assembler + header spec" assigned to jon, grace, chen

jon: Thanks — will ping when PR is up.

grace: Thanks all.

mikaela: End of thread.
